methods.name: Reset
methods.behaviour: l_alu.initialize(); a_alu.initialize(); the objects are kept

methods.name: Calc
methods.signature: function int Calc(int in1, int in2, alu_op_t operation)
methods.behaviour: pick the ALU by code range; load in1 into operand_A and in2 into operand_B (D-002); set alu_op; call execute(); return alu_result

control.then: $error naming the code; return 0; no ALU state changes

locals.name: alu
locals.why: one load/execute path for both ALUs through the virtual execute() (D-012)

spec_text.FR-008: Define a CPU class that contains logical and arithmetic ALU objects.
spec_text.FR-009: Provide a Reset method in CPU.
spec_text.FR-010: Provide CPU.Calc accepting in1 (int), in2 (int), and operation (enum), and returning Result (int).
spec_text.IF-012: CPU.Calc: function int Calc(int in1, int in2, alu_op_t operation)
spec_text.D-002: in1/operand_A is the first operand, in2/operand_B the second. Binary ops compute A op B; SUB is A - B. Port-B ops (SEL_B, INC_B, DEC_B) use operand_B only.
spec_text.D-008: CPU.Reset() calls initialize() on l_alu and a_alu. It does not re-create the objects.
spec_text.D-009: Codes 4'b1110 and 4'b1111 are invalid. Calc returns 0, sets alu_result = 0 in neither ALU, and prints an $error naming the code. No state changes.
spec_text.D-012: function int Calc(int in1, int in2, alu_op_t operation). Codes 0000-0110 go to a_alu, 0111-1101 to l_alu. Calc loads operands and op into that ALU, calls its execute(), returns its alu_result.
spec_text.D-018: CPU.new() constructs l_alu and a_alu; base_alu.new() calls initialize(), so no object is ever used uninitialised.
